note.question: Should a manufacturer collect market data itself or buy data-driven insights from its e-commerce platform when it offers both MTO and C2M customization, and when will the platform participate?
note.overview: A manufacturer and an e-commerce platform play an explicit eight-stage sequential game over whether customization insights are internally collected or purchased, platform participation, data effort and service fees, product design, delivery, and prices. The paper solves unique equilibria by backward induction.

models.method: The paper derives Hotelling demands for the three products, solves the eight-stage game by backward induction for each data route, compares firm payoffs to recover endogenous sourcing and platform-support choices, and evaluates data effort, customization, and customer welfare.

sources.quote: It points out that when the marginal cost of data acquisition is below another given threshold and customers are more sensi­ tive to data breach risks under MTO customization than that under C2M customization, the e-commerce plat­ form may not offer data-driven insights to support the manufacturer’s C2M customization.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Stage 1: the manufacturer chooses internal collection or purchasing platform insights. Stage 2, if purchasing is selected: the platform chooses whether to offer insight support. Stage 3: the manufacturer chooses effort tau_m after internal collection or platform refusal, whereas the platform chooses effort tau_e after accepting collaboration. Stage 4 in the accepted platform route: the platform sets its per-unit insight-service fee.

components.label: Unique subgame-perfect equilibrium of the eight-stage customization and data-sourcing game
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique subgame-perfect equilibrium of the eight-stage customization and data-sourcing game. The authors solve the downstream customer, pricing, delivery, customization, service-fee, data-effort, support, and sourcing decisions backward. Lemma 1 states that unique equilibria exist in both manufacturer-collected and platform-initiated scenarios, and Table 3 reports the equilibrium outcomes.
